summary: Three-dimensional Gaussian splatting is a way of representing a captured place as millions of small, semi-transparent, oriented ellipsoids, each carrying a size, an orientation, an opacity and a set of spherical-harmonic colour terms, drawn by sorting them and blending them rather than by shading surfaces; the four-dimensional work extends it to moving scenes. This record scores the technique together with the file formats that carry it, because for a standards audience the formats are the interoperable part: uncompressed PLY as the source and interchange format, SOG and Streamed SOG as quantised web-delivery formats with published specifications, Niantic's SPZ as a compressed single file, and binary glTF through KHR_gaussian_splatting, which Khronos has ratified, though the compression layer beneath it is contested, with three rival compression extensions open as pull requests against the specification and none merged. The strongest finding is the gap between the research and the wire: three separate well-cited lines of four-dimensional work model time inside the representation, through predicted per-frame deformation, through primitives that are genuinely four-dimensional, and through temporal opacity with per-primitive motion, and not one shipping format has a time axis. What ships instead is a numbered run of complete still frames played back like a flipbook, at whatever frame rate the playing script is set to, with the reference implementation of the best-known four-dimensional paper exporting exactly that; the maintainer of the main open editor has published the design for a proper four-dimensional format and its runtime encoding is still marked to be done. The second finding is that the family disagrees with itself about the coordinate frame, right up, back in SPZ against right, down, front in typical PLY and left, up, front in glTF, and an unstated frame is written through unconverted, so a file that survives a round trip can still come back mirrored. The third is what is entirely missing: no format carries a licence, an authorship record or a signature, which is a strange thing for a representation whose whole purpose is photographing real places and the people in them, and none carries units, so nothing states whether a captured room is two metres across or two hundred. Two traps for anyone planning to build on this. The reference implementation from Inria and the Max Planck Institute is licensed for research and evaluation only, not for commercial use, so several published results cannot legally be shipped as they stand, and the permissively licensed reimplementations must be checked one by one. And MPEG has started coding this representation inside its point-cloud standards, with a Gaussian splat profile amendment to video-based point cloud compression already at committee draft stage, which means a second, unrelated family of splat containers is arriving from a different direction.

coverage.note: The technique carries its own rasteriser: anisotropic three-dimensional Gaussians are projected to screen ellipses, sorted by depth and alpha-blended in one pass, and the glTF carriage requires the primitive to be drawn as points. What is missing is everything above the single draw: no pass structure, no render graph and no statement anywhere in the formats about where the splat pass sits relative to opaque or transparent geometry.
